review.assessment:
The task requires implementing a `flatten` function that respects a `depth` argument (defaulting to 1), stopping recursion after the specified number of levels. The diff introduces a new `solution.mjs` containing a recursive implementation. It iterates over input arrays, recursively calls itself on nested arrays while decrementing depth, and concatenates results. While it correctly sets up the iteration and reduction structure, it completely omits any conditional check to halt recursion when `depth <= 0`. This causes the function to recurse indefinitely until all nesting is exhausted, effectively ignoring the depth argument entirely.

Scope & Change extent: The diff replaces `solution.mjs` with a complete recursive flatten implementation. It covers the structural requirement of writing the function but fails to implement the core behavioral contract of respecting finite depth limits.

Defects:
1. Missing base case / termination condition on `depth`. The recursion proceeds unconditionally whenever an array item is encountered, decrementing `depth` into negative values and flattening all nested levels regardless of the specified limit.
   - call: `node -e "import('./solution.mjs').then(m => console.log(JSON.stringify(m.flatten([1,[2,[3]]]))))"`
   - expected: `[1,2,[3]]` (default depth 1)
   - actual: `[1,2,3]`

The provided implementation lacks the `depth <= 0` check that should guard recursive calls. Adding this condition before recursing into nested arrays will align the behavior with the stated requirements.
